# `role_grant_exceeded`: a role's code reaches a capability its grant leaves out

In an `@[endpoints]` protocol, `role R needs IO.X, ...` is that role's grant:
the body passed to `run_R`, and everything it calls, may use only those
capabilities, the way `main`'s parameters bound the whole program. This error
points at a use outside the grant and, when it can, labels each call from the
body to it.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  needs IO
  needs IO.Console
  needs IO.FileWrite
  needs Session.Live

  @[endpoints]
  protocol Stream do
    role Cons needs IO.Console
    Prod -> Cons : Int
  end

  fn main(c : Cap(IO)) do
    let _ = Stream_Run.run_Cons(c, "cons", "secret", Stream_Run.addrs_from_env(),
      fn (s, con, st) ->
        Stream_Cons.recv_Msg_Prod_Cons_1(s, st, fn (n, st1) ->
          let _ = file_write("/tmp/n", int_to_string(n))
          Stream_Cons.close(s, st1)))
    ()
  end
end
```

The body of role `Cons` writes a file, but `Cons` is granted only
`IO.Console`.

## The fix

Add the capability to the grant. The body receives one `Cap` per granted
capability, in the order the grant lists them, between the session capability
and the state, so widening the grant also adds a parameter to the body (and to
any function the body passes its capabilities to):

```march
mod Main do
  needs IO
  needs IO.Console
  needs IO.FileWrite
  needs Session.Live

  @[endpoints]
  protocol Stream do
    role Cons needs IO.Console, IO.FileWrite
    Prod -> Cons : Int
  end

  fn main(c : Cap(IO)) do
    let _ = Stream_Run.run_Cons(c, "cons", "secret", Stream_Run.addrs_from_env(),
      fn (s, con, fw, st) ->
        Stream_Cons.recv_Msg_Prod_Cons_1(s, st, fn (n, st1) ->
          let _ = file_write("/tmp/n", int_to_string(n))
          Stream_Cons.close(s, st1)))
    ()
  end
end
```

Or remove the use, if the role should not have that authority.

## Why the rule exists

A role's grant is what a deployment of that role is allowed to do. Reading the
protocol tells an operator the most each role's process can do, so a role that
writes files must say so there, however deep the write is.

See also: [the language reference](../capabilities.md).
